reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh actively saving and helping the Hebrew people. The passage states: 'And Yahweh saved Israel that day' (וַיּ֧וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֛ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל). Furthermore, Saul refers to Yahweh as 'the one who saves Israel' (הַמּוֹשִׁ֙יעַ֙ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל). Jonathan's statement that 'there is no restraint for Yahweh to save by many or by few' (כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לַֽיהוָה֙ מַעְצ֔וֹר לְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ) reinforces Yahweh's capacity and willingness to help Israel. The entire narrative arc demonstrates divine intervention on behalf of the Hebrew people in battle.
